items.claim: The header-class contrast this row offers is byte-false as a discriminator: the seeing-verb clause it treats as distinctive to this header is byte-identical in both superscriptions, leaving only the head noun to carry the distinction.
items.evidence: Every pointed run in the row re-collates at byte tier against its cited verse, and the span is byte-sound: MT 1:1 opens with the header noun חֲזוֹן֙ (byte tier) and carries no imperative, vocative, or divine-speech frame anywhere in its bytes - the verse is a header noun, a relative clause, and a four-king regnal list, so the ground for isolating it holds. The defect is in the header-class account: the relative clause אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה re-collates at BYTE tier against MT 2:1 as well, so the seeing-verb is shared by both superscriptions and is not distinctive to this one; the only distinguishing element is the head noun חֲזוֹן֙ against MT 2:1's הַדָּבָר֙. The companion header decision at MT 2:1 states the shared seeing-verb fact correctly, so two accounts of the same bytes disagree inside one cluster. Separately, disclosure-relevant rather than a row error: the fourth regnal name in this row's own verse is יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ (byte tier), the yod-initial byform, attested at exactly one verse in the book (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton, yod-initial spelling) against 29 verses of the yod-less spelling; staged book guidance treats the yod-initial byform as unattested in Isaiah, and the bytes of this verse contradict that. No parashah mark falls in the span and none is claimed; no ketiv/qere note falls anywhere in this chapter.

byte (relative-clause identity MT 1:1 = MT 2:1)

items.claim: The load-bearing ground for this cut - that the summons couplet names no offense yet - is contradicted by the bytes of the row's own first verse, and a catchword straddling its closing seam is undisclosed.
items.evidence: The onset splice שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ re-collates at byte tier and stands at tokens 1-4 of MT 1:2, and the imperative pairing is supportable from the pointed bytes (plural form to the heavens, feminine-singular form to אֶ֔רֶץ) together with both witnesses' renderings, so the onset itself is sound. But MT 1:2 closes וְהֵ֖ם פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי (byte tier): the rebellion charge is stated inside the row's own first verse, so 'before any content of the charge is stated' and 'verses 2-3 name no offense yet' are both byte-false; that rebellion root recurs at MT 1:28 and runs to 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses, skeleton, rebellion-root family). Second, בָּנִים֙ at MT 1:2 recurs as בָּנִ֖ים at MT 1:4 (accent_stripped tier between the two sites; sweep: 14 verses, skeleton, bare plural noun) - a catchword straddling this row's own closing seam, undisclosed, arguing continuity into MT 1:4 against the cut. The lawsuit-vocabulary contrast the row draws outside its span does check out in the bytes: MT 3:13 reads נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה with לָדִ֥ין following (byte tier), so that device distinction is sound. The seam survives on the verse-initial ה֣וֹי at MT 1:4 (byte tier), which is why this is graded medium rather than high.
tier_citations: byte (onset splice; rebellion clause; MT 3:13 lawsuit vocabulary)
accent_stripped (plural-noun catchword MT 1:2 = MT 1:4)
skeleton (rebellion-root sweep 18 verses; plural-noun sweep 14 verses)

items.claim: A catchword pair crosses this row's closing seam undisclosed while the decision on the far side of that same seam argues its opening from the very same device - an asymmetric disclosure across one shared seam.
items.evidence: The row's own byte claims verify: ה֣וֹי is verse-initial at MT 1:4 (byte tier) and its role reading as an opening indictment rather than a woe-oracle onset matches the byte role-split, and קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל at MT 1:4 (byte tier) is a genuine site of the book's signature divine title (sweep: 25 title verses). The parashah citation is correct in type and complete for the span - the setumah at oshb:Isa.1.9 is the only marked verse inside 1:4-1:9, single-witness, tier-3, and correctly barred from driving the boundary. The defect is cross-seam disclosure: MT 1:9 closes כִּסְדֹ֣ם הָיִ֔ינוּ לַעֲמֹרָ֖ה and MT 1:10 carries its vocatives קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם and עַ֥ם עֲמֹרָֽה (byte tier at each cited verse). Those two place-name skeletons stand at 4 and 3 verses book-wide respectively (sweep: 4 verses / 3 verses, skeleton) and fall in adjacent verses only here - a catchword hook at an oracle join, straddling this row's own closing seam and undisclosed, though the decision immediately downstream argues its opening from it. Minor, and translation-carried: the row labels MT 1:9 a remnant note, but the Hebrew there is שָׂרִ֖יד (byte tier), a different root from the book's four-way remnant family; the label rides on the English rendering, though the row's signal keys correctly avoid a remnant claim.

items.claim: A two-site, book-wide word pair carrying its two governing verbs in inverted order straddles this row's closing seam undisclosed, arguing an address running unbroken past the cut.
items.evidence: The onset verifies: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם is byte tier and verse-initial at MT 1:10, and the addressee shift is byte-carried by the two vocatives rather than inferred. The row's recurrence handling is exemplary and independently confirmed here: שִׁמְע֤וּ of MT 1:2 matches MT 1:10 at accent_stripped tier only, and the row explicitly refuses a byte-identical claim while labelling the form contrast as byte-checkable - correct on both counts. The parashah citation is correct in type and span-complete (setumah at oshb:Isa.1.17, the only marked verse inside 1:10-1:17, single-witness, tier-3). The defect: MT 1:17 closes שִׁפְט֣וּ יָת֔וֹם רִ֖יבוּ אַלְמָנָֽה and MT 1:23 carries יָתוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁפֹּ֔טוּ וְרִ֥יב אַלְמָנָ֖ה (byte tier at each cited verse) - the same two nouns with their governing verbs in inverted order. The orphan noun occurs at exactly 2 verses in the whole book and the widow noun at 3 (sweep: 2 verses / 3 verses, skeleton); across those two sites the orphan token matches at accent_stripped tier and the widow token at skeleton tier. A book-wide two-site pair with inverted verb order, straddling the row's own closing seam, is precisely the catchword class that owes disclosure, and it argues a larger bracket reaching past MT 1:17 against this cut.

items.claim: The frame-ownership ground for this seam is carried by the English rendering alone, sits nowhere near the seam in the bytes, and recurs mid-verse inside the block immediately upstream that the row contrasts itself against.
items.evidence: The onset itself is sound: לְכוּ נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה is byte tier and occupies tokens 1-3 of MT 1:18, and the closing כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר is byte tier and verse-final at MT 1:20. But the row grounds the cut on the verse opening a speech-act framed by its own says-Yahweh signature, and no Hebrew form is quoted for that frame anywhere in the row - the frame claim rests on the English. In the bytes the form is יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה, standing at tokens 4-5 of 16 in MT 1:18, so it is not at the seam and frames nothing there; the same quotative sits mid-verse at MT 1:11 as יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה, tokens 5-6 of 17, inside the immediately upstream block, and the two match at accent_stripped tier. Naming the object before the digit: the bare imperfect quotative with the tetragrammaton is attested at exactly 5 verses (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton - MT 1:11, 1:18, 33:10, 41:21, 66:9), and must not be blended with the 5 vav-prefixed narrative sites (MT 3:16, 7:3, 8:1, 8:3, 20:3); on that object the form cannot discriminate an onset from a mid-unit interjection, and here it leans against the row. Separately, the closing formula is called a recognized oracle-closing signature with neither tier label nor digit: that three-word closing skeleton is attested at 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton - MT 1:20, 40:5, 58:14), and only MT 1:20 carries the ki-form. Parashah citation correct in type and span-complete (setumah at oshb:Isa.1.20, single-witness, tier-3). The seam survives on the verse-initial imperative, which holds this at medium.

accent_stripped (quotative MT 1:11 = MT 1:18)

items.claim: The decision and every tier label verify exactly as written, but the one ground offered against the rival division - that the divine-speech signature at MT 1:24 is postpositive and not an onset - is contested by that form's byte position.
items.evidence: Verified in full: all four pointed runs re-collate at byte tier at their cited verses; אֵיכָה֙ is verse-initial at MT 1:21; and the bracket claim is exactly right - קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה of MT 1:21 collates against MT 1:26, and קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה of MT 1:26 against MT 1:21, at skeleton tier in both directions and no higher, since the closing-word accent differs and survives accent-stripping. That matches the row's own skeleton-tier labelling and its two-verse digit (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton, two-word designation). The petuchah at oshb:Isa.1.23 is typed correctly, never conflated with the setumah sites, and is the only marked verse inside the span; the rival it supports is disclosed rather than buried, and the confidence is honestly reduced. The exclamation ה֚וֹי at MT 1:24 is genuinely non-initial (token 8 of 12) and governs a first-person divine action, so the self-exclamation reading holds against a woe-against-addressee reading. The contested point: the row defeats the rival 23|24 division partly by calling the signature postpositive and not an onset frame in itself, but נְאֻ֤ם stands at token 2 of 12 in MT 1:24, immediately after לָכֵ֗ן and ahead of the quoted speech, so at this site it heads the speech rather than following it. Across the book's 23 signature verses (sweep: 23 verses, skeleton) only MT 56:8, where נְאֻם֙ is verse-initial, places the form earlier; every other site sits at token 3 or later. The stated rejection ground is therefore weaker than written, and it leans toward the rival that the tier-3 mark also points to. Available and unused: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה is byte-identical at MT 1:25 and MT 1:26 - a byte-tier anaphora stronger than the skeleton-tier bracket, but lying wholly on the far side of the rival cut, so it does not answer it.
tier_citations: byte (all four row splices; anaphora MT 1:25 = MT 1:26)
skeleton (two-word bracket MT 1:21 = MT 1:26 in both directions; signature-verse sweep 23 verses; bracket sweep 2 verses)
tier-3 parashah, single-witness (petuchah at oshb:Isa.1.23, correctly typed; span-complete)

items.claim: The row asserts its opening seam carries no explicit lexical frame marker; in the bytes a two-term pair that co-occurs in only two verses of this chapter sits at exactly this row's opening verse and the preceding unit's opening verse.
items.evidence: Sound parts first: צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה is byte tier and verse-initial at MT 1:27; the discourse-mode shift is byte-carried, since MT 1:25-26 run first-person cohortatives and MT 1:27 does not; and the setumah at oshb:Isa.1.31 is correctly typed, single-witness, tier-3, the only marked verse in the span. The defect is the asserted absence of a lexical marker at the 26|27 seam. Naming the objects: the bare justice noun stands at MT 1:17, MT 1:21 and MT 1:27 (accent_stripped tier across the three; sweep: 40 verses, skeleton), and the righteousness root runs צֶ֛דֶק at MT 1:21, הַצֶּ֔דֶק at MT 1:26 and בִּצְדָקָֽה at MT 1:27 (byte tier at each cited verse). The two terms co-occur within a single verse at 16 verses book-wide, and inside this chapter at exactly two - MT 1:21 and MT 1:27 (sweep: 16 verses book-wide / 2 verses in the chapter, skeleton, co-occurrence object). This row's opening verse therefore repeats the term-pair of the preceding unit's opening verse across the very seam the row calls unmarked: a byte-true device straddling the row's own opening seam, undisclosed, arguing a bracket from MT 1:21 through MT 1:27 against the cut - and it lands on the seam the row itself grades weakest. Second and smaller: the pointed splice for the closing verse stops at וּבָעֲר֧וּ while the English paired with it runs on through the burning and the unquenched fire, which in the Hebrew is שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם יַחְדָּ֖ו וְאֵ֥ין מְכַבֶּֽה and lies outside the quoted run, so quote and gloss are not cut to the same extent.

items.claim: The shared-feature claim across the two headers ships without tier labels, and its parts sit at three different tiers - one byte-identical, one accent-stripped-only, one skeleton-only.
items.evidence: The row's own onset verifies: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה is byte tier and verse-initial at MT 2:1, the head-noun contrast against MT 1:1's חֲזוֹן֙ is byte-true, and the verse carries no imperative, vocative, or divine-speech frame in its bytes, so the isolation ground holds. The upstream parashah citation is correct in type (setumah at oshb:Isa.1.31, single-witness, tier-3), and no mark falls inside the one-verse span - absence correctly left as no evidence either way. The defect is tier discipline on a recurrence claim asserted flatly. The relative clause אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה re-collates against MT 1:1 at byte tier, so that half of the claim is byte-true; the patronymic is not - MT 1:1 reads בֶן אָמ֔וֹץ and MT 2:1 reads בֶּן אָמ֑וֹץ, differing in the dagesh of the construct form and in the accent on the name, and matching at skeleton tier only; and the seer's name יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ matches MT 2:1 at accent_stripped tier. One unlabelled sentence therefore folds three tiers into a single assertion where the tier is owed at write time, and the strongest half of that evidence - the byte-identical relative clause - goes uncited as such, which is also what makes the competing account of the same clause at the other header verse detectable.
tier_citations: byte (header onset at MT 2:1; head noun at MT 1:1; relative clause MT 1:1 = MT 2:1)
accent_stripped (seer's name MT 1:1 = MT 2:1)
skeleton (patronymic MT 1:1 = MT 2:1)
